documents.title: Faculty Resources for Artificial Intelligence (AI) / Generative AI
documents.summary: A faculty resource page from the Learning and Educational Center that advises instructors to write a syllabus AI policy, explain it to students and discuss it often. It warns against detectors, recommends restructuring courses, and covers privacy, ethics, access and career readiness. It sets no binding rule for students and points to a separate university AI policy.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no stance on student AI use; it says "Effectively integrating Generative AI requires both proactive conversations with students and a clear syllabus policy" and leaves the content of the policy to each instructor, so it delegates.

documents.title: Student Handbook 2025-2026: Academic Standards (generative AI clause)
documents.summary: The handbook's academic standards section bans students' use of generative AI on coursework and assessments without prior faculty permission. Only this sentence in the handbook addresses AI; it sits within the original-work standard.
documents.stance_why: AI is "expressly prohibited" on coursework "without the prior permission of their faculty member", so it is banned unless permitted, which is restrict.

units.why: The handbook says "use of generative artificial intelligence ... without the prior permission of their faculty member ... is expressly prohibited", so AI is banned unless faculty permit it, a fallback-style rule (P06); P06 chosen over P01 because permission is the exception.

units.fit_note: Applies to all coursework and assessments university-wide, not only when a syllabus is silent.

units.why: The sentence also prohibits AI use "in any way that violates the academic standards of NSU and/or a student’s academic program", a limit even where permission exists; P36 fits as misuse is tied to academic standards.

notes: Only the Academic Standards original-work clause in the handbook mentions generative AI.
